rationale: Round-2 grounding audit of 747bf9b3. MY ROUND-1 ASK: ADDRESSED — the prospective-snapshot protocol delivers everything the ask named: untracked files are staged into snapshot tree T by the temp-index `add -A` (closing the DiffNameOnlyRef blindness), BOTH gates measure base→T through the new ChangedFilesTree leg with gate inputs read from T:path, the unqualified measurement-equivalence prose is gone from plan and amendment (replaced by the commit-IS-T construction), and fixture leg (i) is exactly the new-untracked-file refusal case I asked for, with (ii)-(iv) covering the hook/export/interval holes I had only footnoted. The protocol's fresh grounding claims all re-derive TRUE at HEAD: commitWithExport's `git add -A` comment at mindspec_executor.go:1484 with the bd export at :1491 running before staging (:1494 gitutil.CommitAll); ChangedFiles' empty-base leg at :1208-1210 delegating to cwd-rooted DiffNameOnlyRef("", head) and the two-ref leg rooted `git -C g.Root` at :1221; docsync.go:76-78's base=="" → HEAD~1 default unaffected; CommitTreeMerge (gitops.go:986) and UpdateRef (gitops.go:222) exist as the cited 127 plumbing precedent; FileAtRef exists and worktrees share the object store, so T:path reads work cross-checkout; G2's ahead-of-preflight sites are exactly impl.go:277, plan.go:300, complete.go:522 (EnsureMigrated/WithCache), and the ADR-0034 EnsureMigrated pattern (migrate.go) is the real template for EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2; G5's #245 call-graph is accurate (cmd/mindspec/complete.go:145 completeTail on the sole success return, :157 FormatResult first, 'Bead %s closed.' at internal/complete/complete.go:1380). HOWEVER, one NEW correctness hole in the delivered recipe blocks approval: the snapshot step as written builds T from an EMPTY temp index. GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at a fresh temp path is an empty index; `add -A -- . ':!<named-artifact>'` then stages everything EXCEPT the excluded ADR-0025 artifact, so T simply LACKS .beads/issues.jsonl — a TRACKED file present in the parent tip. `git commit-tree T -p <tip>` therefore materializes a user commit that DELETES the tracker artifact from the bead branch. When artifactDirt was empty at the dirty-scan (no bd delta this run), NO sync commit follows to restore it, and the deletion merges bead→spec — silent loss of the tracked ADR-0025 artifact; even when the sync commit does follow, the branch carries a spurious delete/re-add pair and base→T diffs list the artifact as deleted. The fix is one step: SEED the temp index from the bead tip (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git read-tree <tip>` before the `add -A`), so the excluded artifact rides in T at its tip state — exclusion then means 'unchanged', not 'absent' — which also keeps deletions-of-tracked-files semantics intact (read-tree stages them; add -A removes them). A second, smaller gap: after the fast-forward update-ref moves the checked-out bead branch to the commit-from-T, the REAL index is never reconciled — newly-tracked files appear as phantom staged deletions (in HEAD, absent from the stale index), so exec.Status-based surfaces (the residual-dirt WARN at complete.go:928-933) emit spurious paths and fixture (iv)'s 'stays dirt' assertion gets polluted. CommitPaths itself is safe (pathspec-limited `git commit -- <paths>`, gitops.go:1699, so phantoms never enter the sync commit), but the plan should pin an index refresh (e.g. `git -C wtPath reset --quiet --mixed` / read-tree HEAD — index only, worktree untouched) after the ref move. Both fixes are sentences in bead 6, not redesigns; the protocol is otherwise sound and I expect to approve once the seeding step is pinned. All other round-1-fix grounding in my lens verifies: G3's flock/journal idiom claims, G4's SanctionedDerivedSync single-caller fence (impl-adopt house pattern exists), the two-surface release wording correction, and the writer-inventory/next-new-writer/release-redesign claims from round 1 are unchanged and remain true.
concrete_changes_required: Bead 6 step 1 (and the OQ-1 protocol paragraph + fixture (iii) as needed): seed the temporary index from the bead branch tip BEFORE the exclusion-bearing `add -A` — `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git -C wtPath read-tree <tip>` then `add -A -- . ':!<named-artifact>'` then `write-tree`. Without the seed the temp index starts EMPTY, the pathspec exclusion makes the tracked ADR-0025 artifact ABSENT from T, and `commit-tree T -p <tip>` materializes a commit that deletes .beads/issues.jsonl from the bead branch (silently merged to spec whenever artifactDirt was empty and no sync commit follows). State that with the seed, exclusion means unchanged-at-tip rather than absent, and add a fixture leg asserting the user commit's diff vs tip NEVER touches the named artifact.

Bead 6 step 4: after the fast-forward update-ref of the checked-out bead branch, reconcile the REAL index to the new HEAD (index-only refresh, e.g. `git reset --quiet --mixed` in wtPath; worktree untouched). Otherwise newly-tracked-via-T files appear as phantom staged deletions in the stale index, exec.Status-based surfaces (residual-dirt WARN, complete.go:928-933) report spurious paths, and fixture (iv)'s interval-edit-stays-dirt assertion is polluted. Note CommitPaths is already safe (pathspec-limited commit, gitops.go:1699).

findings.claim: Snapshot step: 'GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git -C wtPath add -A -- . ':!<named-artifact>'' + write-tree → T; commit created FROM T so committed ≡ measured by construction.
findings.evidence: A GIT_INDEX_FILE pointing at a nonexistent temp path is an EMPTY index; the exclusion pathspec keeps the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl out of the staging, so T lacks a file present in <tip>'s tree, and `commit-tree T -p <tip>` yields a commit deleting it. The sync commit (CommitPaths, pathspec-scoped) restores it ONLY when artifactDirt was non-empty at the scan; otherwise the deletion lands and merges. NEW_ISSUE introduced by the round-1 fix; fixed by read-tree seeding from <tip>.

findings.claim: Step 3's side-effect claim ('worktree, real index, and refs untouched') is true for the SNAPSHOT, but the plan is silent on the real index after the ff update-ref moves the checked-out bead branch.
findings.evidence: update-ref does not touch the real index; files newly tracked via T show as staged deletions (HEAD-vs-index) until refreshed. exec.Status consumers (complete.go:928-933 residual-dirt WARN) and fixture (iv) observe phantom entries. CommitPaths is unaffected (git commit -- <paths>, gitops.go:1699).
